questions.question: Q: Name the four components of an effective warm-up.

points.text: Pulse-raising activities, joint mobilisation, dynamic stretching and dance-specific movement preparation.

questions.question: Q: Why is a cool-down important after dancing?

points.text: A cool-down gradually lowers the heart rate, prevents blood pooling, reduces muscle soreness and maintains flexibility through static stretching.

questions.question: Q: What is the difference between a sprain and a strain?

points.text: A sprain is damage to a ligament (joint connector), usually from twisting; a strain is damage to a muscle or tendon, usually from overstretching or overuse.

questions.question: Q: How does nutrition affect a dancer's performance?

points.text: Carbohydrates provide energy for dancing, protein supports muscle repair, and calcium and vitamin D maintain bone health — poor nutrition leads to fatigue, weakness and increased injury risk.

questions.question: Q: Give three features of a safe rehearsal environment.

points.text: A sprung floor to absorb impact, adequate ventilation and temperature control, and clear, unobstructed space free of hazards.
